obligations.title: Run the gate that covers this change
obligations.question: Each site names its coveringGate — the gate over the artifact this change invalidates. You do not choose it and must not answer about a different one (ADR 0098). Determine wiredBy for that gate by reading, not running — grep the .husky hooks, the .github/workflows jobs, and the yarn gates:run manifest (tools/scripts/run-assertion-gates.mjs) at the head commit for the gate's script name, and write the one that invokes it, or "none" if nothing does (ADR 0074). command and exitCode are optional: record them only when you also ran the checker's own script directly through node, never through yarn or corepack yarn; when you did not run it, write "not run" in both. Cite wiredBy: the file, the line number, and the exact text of the line that invokes the gate; a wiredBy of "none" carries no citation, because nowhere has no line.
obligations.defect: wiredBy "none" is a finding: per ADR 0074 the checker is not a gate, so nothing would have caught this on main. A non-zero exitCode, when one was obtained, is also a finding, with the command and exit code as executed evidence — raised the ordinary way (an obligation answer that exposes a defect is written up like any other finding), not mechanically by defectWhen, because exitCode is optional and its "not run" value cannot be told apart from a real code by a plain equality check.

obligations.title: A destructive confirmation names everything it destroys
obligations.question: For each site: follow the confirmed code path and list every persisted key, store, or record it writes or clears; quote the confirmation text verbatim; then state whether the text names everything in that list. Do not infer the mutation set from the handler's name. Cite confirmationText: the file, the line number, and the exact text of the line the message starts on.
obligations.defect: namesEverything false is a finding. A whole-vault or whole-account destructive action behind a bare window.confirm rather than a dialog is also a finding.

obligations.title: Injected props land on the control, not on a wrapper
obligations.question: For each site: name the element that is the direct child of the Slot-based component, state where the injected id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid land, and state whether that element is the focusable control the user types into. Cite slotChild: the file, the line number, and the exact text of the direct child's own line — that line, not the Slot-based component's.
obligations.defect: isFocusableControl false is a finding: Radix Slot forwards its props to its single direct child, so a wrapper element between FormControl and the input takes the label association and the input is announced by its placeholder or not at all.

obligations.title: An environment assignment stores what it looks like it stores
obligations.question: For each site: quote the right-hand side of the assignment as written, state the value actually stored after the process.env setter coerces it, and state whether that is what the surrounding code reads as intending. Cite assignedExpression: the file, the line number, and the exact text of the assignment line.
obligations.defect: matchesIntent false is a finding. Assigning undefined or null to unset a variable is the common shape: the setter coerces to string, so the key holds the truthy literal "undefined". delete is what unsets it.

obligations.title: A fan-out over a guarded enum covers every member
obligations.question: Each site touches a guarded domain enum — one enum:fanout:check guards (ADR 0053) — either by adding a member where the enum is defined or by adding a consumer that names its members. Name the enum and list its members as defined at the head commit. Then list every scope at the head commit, inside the diff or not, that enumerates those members — on the enum (VaultBlobType.Tasks), as property names (data.tasks), or as string literals — and say for each whether it reaches the pinned satisfies Record<…> table or enumerates the members by hand. For a member added to the enum, the consumers are the code that already fanned out over it, which the diff usually does not touch; for a new consumer, it is the site's own scope. A test file that lists members as fixtures is not a consumer. Answer omission with the first hand-enumerating scope that leaves a member out, naming the member it leaves out, or "none" if every hand-enumeration covers every member. Cite omission: the file, the line number, and the exact text of one of that scope's enumeration lines; "none" carries no citation. Answer wiredBy about the site's coveringGate exactly as for run-the-gate-that-covers-this-change: by reading, not running — grep the .husky hooks, the .github/workflows jobs, and tools/scripts/run-assertion-gates.mjs at the head commit for its script name, and write the one that invokes it, or "none" if nothing does (at a head that predates the checker, nothing does). Cite wiredBy: the file, the line number, and the exact text of the invoking line; "none" carries no citation. A finding raised for this entry carries ruleId obligation-enum-fanout-omits-a-member and is anchored in the site's own file, naming the omitting scope and the member in its text.
obligations.defect: An omission other than "none" while wiredBy is "none" is a finding: a hand-enumerated consumer that leaves out a member of a guarded enum drops that member silently — for VaultBlobType, User-owned ciphertext, with no error and no recovery (ADR 0033) — and per ADR 0074 nothing at this head would have caught it. When wiredBy names a line, the gate already fails any hand-enumeration of a guarded enum, so the omission is redundant (ADR 0074): count it in suppressedRedundant instead.
